input.quote: (h) Neither Party may assign (voluntarily, by operation of law, or otherwise) this Agreement or any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the other Party's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, provided however, that either Party may assign this Agreement without approval or consent to any affiliate or purchaser of all or substantially all of said Party's assets related to the subject matter of this Agreement or to any successor by way of merger, stock sale, consolidation or similar transaction.
input.rationale: Clause 4(h) gives AP the assignment freedom we require: it may assign without consent to an affiliate, to a purchaser of all or substantially all relevant assets, or to a successor by merger, stock sale or consolidation, and any other assignment requires consent not to be unreasonably withheld. Nothing in the term/termination provisions (p0016) or elsewhere gives Kubient a termination, consent or re-pricing right triggered by a change of control of AP — the document contains no change-of-control trigger at all. The clause is mutual rather than one-way, so it sits at the fallback position (mutual right to assign to successors with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld) rather than the preferred position; the only shortfalls from preferred are the absence of a written-notice requirement and of an express bar on assignment by Kubient to an AP competitor, which are minor sub-elements noted here and not redlined.
